lines.text: “I paid. Here's my screenshot.” That is how customers write to a small online shop: a phone photo of their banking app, in Korean or Japanese.
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, on Nebius Token Factory, reads the photo. The payment, not the balance, not the points, not the phone's clock.
The payment provider's ledger checks it: same amount, same minute. Then the money chain shows the one link where the money got stuck, with the rows that prove it.
Same kind of screen. One number edited.
The ledger has never seen that payment. The model can't spot the edit; the ledger can. The reply politely asks for the card statement, and nothing changes.
Messages are messy too. Two addresses: the account is his wife's, but he paid with his own.
Nemotron 3.5 Lightning reads the message: who is writing, what they claim, which records to look up. Addresses are hidden from the model, and anything the message doesn't say is dropped.
A simple rule would grab the first address and find nothing.
A verifier, not the model, walks the chain. The order was saved under a typo, exmaple dot com, and the mail bounced.
Every call is on screen: which Nemotron did which job, the time, the tokens and the cost. Ultra is called only when the first reading is unsure.
Approve, and the fix runs. On the public demo, only your own copy of the data changes.
Ask for someone else's order, and it is not read. And when nothing was charged, it says so. Nothing is broken. You were never charged.
FILL AFTER MEASURING: e.g. On sixteen phone photos built by a separate agent, Nemotron read the payment right on X; free OCR with rules, three.
Paid, but nothing arrived? Here's the proof, found in one pass.
